title: 367. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Surface Area of Cones
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Lateral area of a right cone
questions.learningObjective: Identify the formula for a cone's curved surface area.
questions.question: A right circular cone has base radius \(r\), perpendicular height \(h\), and slant height \(l\). Which formula gives its lateral surface area?
questions.explanation: Unrolling the curved surface gives a sector of radius \(l\) and arc length \(2\pi r\). Its area is \(\frac{1}{2}l(2\pi r)=\pi rl\).
questions.hint: Think about which cone length becomes the radius of the unrolled sector.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate lateral area from radius and slant height.
questions.question: A right circular cone has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and slant height \(9\text{ cm}\). What is its lateral surface area?
questions.explanation: The lateral area is \(\pi rl=\pi(4)(9)=36\pi\text{ cm}^2\). The value \(16\pi\) is only the base area.
questions.hint: Identify the two lengths used for the curved surface.

questions.learningObjective: Add a cone's base area and lateral area.
questions.question: A closed right circular cone has radius \(5\text{ cm}\) and slant height \(13\text{ cm}\). What is its total surface area, including the base?
questions.explanation: The total is \(\pi rl+\pi r^2=65\pi+25\pi=90\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: List every exposed surface of the closed cone.

questions.learningObjective: Use the Pythagorean theorem before calculating total cone area.
questions.question: A closed right circular cone has radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and perpendicular height \(8\text{ cm}\). What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: The slant height is \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\text{ cm}\). Thus the total area is \(\pi(6)(10)+\pi(6^2)=96\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: First find the length from the apex to the rim.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the material area of a cone without a base.
questions.question: An open conical hat has base diameter \(10\text{ cm}\) and slant height \(12\text{ cm}\). Ignoring seams and waste, how much material covers its curved surface?
questions.explanation: The radius is \(5\text{ cm}\). Only the lateral surface is covered, so the material area is \(\pi(5)(12)=60\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Decide whether the circular opening requires material.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a lateral-area equation for slant height.
questions.question: A right circular cone has radius \(6\text{ cm}\) and lateral area \(48\pi\text{ cm}^2\). What is its slant height?
questions.explanation: From \(6\pi l=48\pi\), the slant height is \(l=8\text{ cm}\). This exceeds the radius, as a nondegenerate right cone requires.
questions.hint: Isolate the unknown length in the lateral-area formula.

questions.learningObjective: Exclude shared bases when calculating exterior area.
questions.question: Two identical right circular cones, each with radius \(3\text{ cm}\) and slant height \(5\text{ cm}\), are joined along their entire circular bases. What is the exterior surface area of the resulting solid?
questions.explanation: Both bases are internal. The exterior consists of two curved surfaces, giving \(2\pi(3)(5)=30\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Identify which surfaces become hidden at the join.

questions.concept: Cone area from a sector net
questions.learningObjective: Recover the radius from a sector and find total cone area.
questions.question: A sector of radius \(10\text{ cm}\) and angle \(288^\circ\) forms a cone's curved surface without overlap. A circular base is then added. What is the total surface area?
questions.explanation: The sector arc is \(\frac{288}{360}(2\pi\cdot10)=16\pi\), so the cone radius is \(8\text{ cm}\). Its lateral area is \(80\pi\), and its base area is \(64\pi\). The total is \(144\pi\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Equate the sector's arc length to the base circumference.

questions.concept: Recovering slant height from total area
questions.learningObjective: Subtract the base area before solving for slant height.
questions.question: A closed right circular cone has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and total surface area \(40\pi\text{ cm}^2\). What is its slant height?
questions.explanation: The base area is \(16\pi\), leaving lateral area \(24\pi\). Thus \(4\pi l=24\pi\), giving \(l=6\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Separate the base contribution from the total area.

questions.concept: Radius from a constrained surface area
questions.learningObjective: Solve a total-area equation with a slant-height constraint.
questions.question: A closed right circular cone has slant height \(l=3r\) and total surface area \(80\pi\text{ cm}^2\). What is its base radius?
questions.explanation: Substitution gives \(\pi r(3r)+\pi r^2=4\pi r^2=80\pi\). Hence \(r^2=20\), and the positive radius is \(2\sqrt{5}\text{ cm}\).
questions.hint: Substitute the length relationship before solving for the radius.
